name: Saint Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi
history: A Carmelite nun of Florence, of one of the city’s great families, whose life of prayer was marked by long ecstasies, recorded word for word by her sisters, and by years of spiritual darkness. She burned with love for God and grief that He was so little loved, and wrote to popes and bishops pleading for the renewal of the Church.
life: Caterina de’ Pazzi was drawn to prayer as a child, made her first Communion at ten and soon after promised herself to God. Against her family’s wishes she entered the Carmelite monastery of Santa Maria degli Angeli in Florence in 1582, taking the name Mary Magdalene. Gravely ill as a novice, she was allowed to make her vows early on a stretcher, and then began a series of ecstasies in which she spoke aloud of the love of God, the Passion and the Holy Spirit; her sisters wrote down what she said, and these records fill several volumes. For five years she endured temptation and dryness, which she called the lions’ den. She served as mistress of novices and subprioress, and was loved for her gentleness. Tradition remembers her crying out that Love is not loved. After a long and painful illness she died in 1607, aged forty-one.
prayerTo: Saint Mary Magdalene de’ Pazzi, you burned with love for God and grieved that Love is not loved. Pray for contemplatives, for all in spiritual darkness, and for the renewal of the Church. Teach me to love God with my whole heart, and to persevere in prayer when it is dry. Amen.
penance: Spend a quarter of an hour in prayer today even if it feels dry, offering the dryness itself. Make an act of love for God for those who never think of Him.
meditation: Love is not loved, she is said to have cried through the cloister. What would it mean for you to love Love today?
prayer: O God, lover of chastity, Who endowed with heavenly gifts blessed Mary Magdalen, a virgin on fire with love for You, grant that we who keep this feast-day in her honor may imitate her by purity and love. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
